deities: Goddess Bahuchara Mata (worshipped as Bala - the child form - through a crystal Bala Yantra)

history.dynasty: Original shrine attributed to king Sankhal Raj (1152 CE); present main temple by Manajirao Gaekwad of Baroda (1783 CE); Maratha-era contributions
history.period: Original shrine 1152 CE (first inscription 1280 CE); major reconstruction 18th century (1783 CE)
history.summary: Major Shakti temple at Bahucharaji (Becharaji), Mehsana district, dedicated to Bahuchara Mata. Per the Bombay Gazetteer the original shrine was built by a king Sankhal Raj in 1152 CE, with the first surviving inscription from 1280 CE. Three shrines: the Adyasthan (original site around a varakhadi tree where the goddess is said to have first appeared), the madhyasthan (18th-century Maratha structure with an incised plaque), and the main temple begun in 1783 CE by Manajirao Gaekwad after the goddess cured him of a tumour (consecration Samvat 1847 / 1791 CE per trust sources). She is worshipped as Bala Bahuchara, carries a rooster as vahan, is counted among Gujarat's Shakti Peethas (a hand of Sati is said to have fallen here), and is the patroness of the hijra community; ~1.5 million pilgrims a year is cited (verify). CSV TOWN/STATE FLAG: CSV row has town 'Mehsana' (the district) and puts the town name in the state column - temple stands at Bahucharaji town, Mehsana district, GUJARAT.

name: Bahucharaji Temple
town_description: Bahucharaji (also Becharaji) is a temple town and taluka place in Mehsana district, north Gujarat, named after the goddess herself. The town grew around the shrine and is one of the three Shakti Peethas of Gujarat, alongside Ambaji and Pavagadh.

travel.road: Bahucharaji town, ~35 km west of Mehsana on the Mehsana-Viramgam road; local buses and taxis available

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Navratri and Purnima days (very crowded)
visitor_information.opening_hours: Darshan reported ~7:00 AM-7:00 PM daily with morning and evening aartis (verify current timings)
